title: Answer every item in the live scorer
statement: After items are built or rebuilt, submit the right answer, each wrong answer and an incomplete one to the live scorer, since scoring that loaded can still be wrong.
example: A behavioural sweep found 41 rebuilt choice items paying 0 for every answer.
detail: A behavioural sweep of a Grade 5 course found 41 choice items paying 0 for every answer, because their scoring compared the response with stale option text instead of the key's id, and the worklog notes that writing a file and reading it back catches only that it landed (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0089-parent-claude-sessions-worklog-2026-07-09.qmd`, lines 180 and 235-236). After the fix, a full re-sweep reported 772/772 paying full credit (the same file, line 238). In a Grade 3 course, a match item's right buckets were keyed twice with a match maximum of 1, which would have let a renderer that follows the spec accept an incomplete response (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0236-g5-package-build-facts-and-g3-fixlist-apply-2026-07-02.qmd`, lines 99-100). Scoring that loaded, or was checked only on the right answer, can still pay nothing, pay for a wrong answer or accept an incomplete one.

Verify JSON health and one actual answer after launch; HTTP200 or environment presence alone is insufficient.
A browser submission on G5-U9-L1/p2 accepted the original playwright explanation and enabled Next page (round-2/g5-u9/dom/probe-playwright-real-scoring.txt).

The scoring sweep was a major lesson. Raw XML read-back was not enough. A set of Unit 2 MCQs had stale literal option text in response processing, causing a response-processing desync. Behavioral scoring caught and fixed 41/41 of those. This became a rule: course-serving means live scoring behavior, not just valid looking QTI.
